newsitem.title: USA: Roger Hershey says leaving Merrill Lynch & Co.
newsitem.headline: Roger Hershey says leaving Merrill Lynch & Co.

text.p: Managing Director Roger Hershey said he has resigned from Merrill Lynch & Co's municipal department effective February 14.
Hershey currently manages Merrill's Municipal Strategies Group. His duties include supervising risk management, some abitrage acitivities and derviatives trading.
Hershey said while Merrill Managing Director Arnold Finkelstein is also leaving, their departures are unlinked.
Finkelstein could not be reached for immediate comment.
Hershey said he had been "toying" with the idea of leaving for some time, but did not make a decision until this Fall.

"It's time. Its been 15 years I've been here, and there have been some changes," Hershey said. "I've done a lot of things I'm very proud of. The business has changed, I've changed, and it's time to look for another challenge."
Hershey said while he has no immediate plans, he is unlikely to "stray far from the business."

"I love the Street, I love the action, I love the markets, I'm always going to be involved with them," he said. "I wanted to kind of do it going out on a high note," he said. "The firm is doing well, the department is doing well. The business is tough, I don't have to tell you it's changing, but I feel pretty good about what we've done here."
Hershey joined Merrill Lynch in 1976 and left in 1983 to start Morgan Stanley & Co's municipal bond trading desk. He spent two years at Morgan, before joining Kidder Peabody & Co.
After nine months, he was hired by EF Hutton to run institutional trading. EF Hutton was subsequently bought out by Shearson, and Merrill Lynch & Co hired Hershey back in 1988.
